notesStmt.note: The letter on the reverse of this manuscript is dated 14 August 1889. In his notes of a visit to the poet on 26 February 1890, Horace Traubel writes that Whitman reported "having sent 'A Twilight Song' to the Century." (See With Walt Whitman in Camden [Carbondale and Edwardsville: Southern Illinois University Press, 1982] 6:311). Therefore, the current manuscript must have been created between these two dates.

The poem represented by this draft was published as "A Twilight Song: For unknown buried soldiers, North and South" in the May 1890 issue of Century Illustrated Monthly Magazine. With minor changes and without the subtitle, it was included in Good-Bye My Fancy (1891) and in the "Good-Bye My Fancy" annex to Leaves of Grass (1891-1892).
